Anya: Heads-up — after the compact-queue refactor I noticed a new pattern: small requests (<=64 tokens) are getting evicted repeatedly when a big burst lands, causing tail latency to spike 4-5x.
Mateo: ugh. Seen similar in canary. Is this the eviction hysteresis we tightened?
Anya: I suspect it's the new 'compactness' pass that merges inflight sets. When a big request arrives it triggers a hard compaction which drains some microbatches and forces tiny streams to re-enqueue.
Raj: can you paste a simple repro trace?
Anya: paste: 
```
--- trace snippet ---
 enqueue(tenant=a, req=small-1)
 enqueue(tenant=b, req=big-1)
 compact_pass(trigger=big-1)
 evict(small-1) -> reenqueue(small-1)
 repeat x3
--- end ---
```
Sophia: Quick thought: we may be conflating two responsibilities — packing for GPU efficiency vs admission fairness. The compact pass was optimized for packing, not fairness.
Mateo: Agree. Two orthogonal knobs: (1) compaction aggressiveness (pack ratio) and (2) eviction policy (soft vs hard). Right now compaction does both.
Anya: Proposed change: split compaction into "pack" and "stabilize" phases. Pack only groups compatible batches; stabilize applies a soft-evict that favors tiny requests for a short grace period.
Raj: How about encoding a per-entry state machine so we can reason about transitions? e.g. {queued, packed, stabilized, evicted}. That would make telemetry explicit.
Sophia: +1. Also add a headroom token on enqueue (an integer) that decays on pack. If headroom>0, entry is immune to hard-evict for Nms.
Mateo: Implementation sketch: add proto field to queue entry: 
```
message QueueEntry {
  string tenant = 1;
  uint64 req_id = 2;
  uint32 tokens = 3; // rough size
  uint32 headroom_ms = 4; // immunity window
  uint32 state = 5; // enum
}
```
Anya: That looks fine. Concern: metadata bloat — we read/write queue entries hot path. Keep fields tiny (u32). Also prefer relative time deltas instead of wall-clock.
Raj: Telemetry: emit transition events with minimal cardinality (tenant, state_from, state_to, delta_ms). That will help validate if small reqs get stabilized.
Sophia: We should also add a fallback: if a tenant's tiny requests see >3 requeues within 200ms, automatically escalate to a per-tenant microqueue for a short window. Microqueues reduce interference cost.
Mateo: Nice. Microqueue could be ephemeral and reclaimed quickly. Need admission credits to avoid starving global throughput.
Anya: Operational concerns: we must expose pack_ratio and headroom_ms via runtime flags + runtime-metric gauges. Also add a simple admin endpoint to dump per-tenant microqueue sizes for incident debugging.
infra-bot: deploy-canary report: canary/compact-refactor v2 rolled at 6210004000 — 10% traffic. 6210004200: increased evict_count for tiny-requests +43%.
Raj: Perfect — infra-bot data confirms the hypothesis. Next steps: 1) implement state field + headroom_ms in queue proto (mateo/anya pair) 2) add stabilize phase with soft-evict heuristic (sophia/raj) 3) telemetry events and admin dump (anya) 4) canary with microqueue escalation enabled.
Sophia: For the RFC follow-up doc: I'll write a short section comparing fairness strategies (headroom, microqueue, token-buckets) and include the state diagram.
Mateo: I'll open a small PR with proto + wire changes and a microbench for pack_ratio x headroom_ms matrix.
Anya: Thanks — prioritize safety: default headroom_ms=0 and stabilize disabled until we have metrics. We can opt-in per-canary.
Raj: I'll own the canary window and SLO alerts. If tails improve we promote.
Anya: ok. tagging next check-in in #eng-runtime in 48h. :thumbsup:
